# Daisy

## Personality

Lively, messy and never seen without paint on her nose, she thinks no colour is too bright. She is cheerfully deaf to compliments.

## Lore

Daisy always has paint on her nose. Nobody knows how it gets there. She does not touch her nose while she works, she swears, and yet by mid-morning there is a dab of sunflower yellow on it, and by evening it has been joined by a smudge of sky blue and a fleck of something pink. She is twenty-two, lively, messy and quick, with her sleeves rolled up and her hair tied back in a rag that used to be a paint cloth, and she believes, with her whole heart, that no colour is ever too bright.

### The houses

Daisy paints the mushroom houses of Kaldemor that her grandfather Bertie shapes. Every spring, when the houses grow and Bertie cuts their new rooms and windows, Daisy follows a week behind with her pots and brushes, and by midsummer the whole town looks as if it has just been unwrapped. She paints the caps in spots and stripes and, once, in checks, which the owner asked her to undo and then asked her to put back. She also paints half the shutters in Kaldemor, the doors of the Sleepy Snail, the sign over Bram's stall and, every autumn, the harvest fair booths.

She mixes her own colours from whatever she can find: crushed petals from the meadow, clay from Mabel's bank, soot, egg, and once a handful of blue snail shell ground fine, which made the brightest blue she has ever had and which she has been trying to get again ever since. She names her colours, too. The yellow on the tall house by the Market steps is called Tuesday. Nobody has ever understood why.

### Bertie and the family

Daisy was born in Kaldemor. Her father, Bertie's son, never cared for mushrooms or for paint, and when Daisy was twelve he and her mother moved to Selsior to keep a shop. They live there still and write at midwinter. Daisy refused to go. She had already painted the henhouse, the gate and her grandmother's best chair, and she said the houses needed her. She stayed with Bertie and her grandmother Heather, and she has stayed ten years. Heather died six years ago, and now it is Daisy and Bertie, and the hat by the door that he still talks to.

She adores her grandfather and teases him without mercy. He never measures; she never plans. Between them, they say, they make one sensible craftsman. Lately she has watched him come home more tired from his spring rounds, and she has started carrying the heavy satchel herself without asking.

### Fen

Little Fen, who carries Bertie's tools, once asked Daisy if she might paint a shutter. Daisy gave her a brush and three pots and walked away, and when she came back the shutter was a colour nobody has been able to name. Daisy thinks it is the best shutter in Kaldemor. She has hung it on her own window.

### Compliments and Jem

Daisy is cheerfully deaf to compliments. Tell her a house is beautiful and she will tell you the left shutter is too green. Tell her she is beautiful and she will ask you to pass the turpentine.

This has made life very hard for Jem the fiddler. For a year now, Jem has been writing a song for Daisy, and for a year it has never been good enough to play to her. He turns up wherever she is working and plays tunes that are nearly the song and then stops. Everybody in the Workshops knows. Bertie knows and is enjoying it enormously. Whether Daisy knows is the great question of the lane. She has never said a word about it. Once, though, she painted the shutters of the Sleepy Snail the exact colour of Jem's fiddle, and when Molly asked her why, she said she had had some brown left over, and then went pink under the paint.

### What she wants and fears

Daisy wants to find that blue again, to paint every house in Kaldemor at least once and to paint something, someday, that nobody has ever seen before. She fears that Bertie will grow too tired for his rounds, and that the houses will grow crooked without him. The houses nearest the woods have started leaning, and she has noticed that the paint on them cracks in the mornings as though they had shivered in the night.

### Hooks

A traveller might be asked to gather blue snail shells from the meadow, so that Daisy can rediscover her lost colour. Another quest might begin the day Jem finally plays his song in the square, and Daisy, for once, does not have paint on her nose, and somebody has to find out where she has gone.
